items.rationale: Sections 2.4.3 and 7.1.7(c) support standard fittings needed to repair the failed indoor heating joint. Four elbows benchmark at €42 gross.

Section 7.1.8(c) and (e) excludes duplicate or undocumented material; a second set of four same-size elbows is not established by the short repair description. If separately needed, four benchmark at €42 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers fittings used in the reinstatement, but §7.1.8(e) requires the 28 mm fittings to be attributable to the documented repair. Five would benchmark at €104 gross if supported.
The short joint repair does not establish the need for five additional bends under §7.1.8(e). If their use is documented, the five-piece benchmark is €103 gross.
A single transition bend is plausible as a necessary fitting under §7.1.7(c), subject to confirming that it was used on the repaired run. The reference supports €21 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) includes ordinary fastenings used in the repair. Eight screws benchmark at €9.30 gross.
Section 7.1.8(e) requires dimensions that match the documented work; no 10 mm pipe is identified. If the clamps are shown to fit the repair, four benchmark at €19.20 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers necessary pipe fixings, and these match the listed 15 mm copper. Four clamps at about €5.20 each total €20.80 gross.
Section 7.1.7(g) covers necessary plumbing labour at customary rates. The reference benchmark for 6.75 hours is €619 gross.
Section 7.1.7(g) permits necessary helper labour, and the claim confirms the helper attended for part of the job. The benchmark for 5.75 hours is €409 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like copper, but §7.1.8(e) requires support for billing 6.4 m when about 1 m was cut out. The full-line benchmark is €99 gross if the billed length is justified.
Section 7.1.7(f) permits the first travel charge for this contractor and invoice. One charge benchmarks at €80 gross.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers installation consumables not already billed elsewhere. The customary lump sum is €43 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) expressly excludes a separate processing charge. The €15 figure is a conditional estimate only.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers like-for-like insulation needed on the repaired run, but the six metres need support under §7.1.8(e). The full-line benchmark is €135 gross.

Sections 7.1.8(c) and (e) bar duplicate or undocumented insulation, and the claim identifies no separate use for the mats beyond the pipe insulation already billed. Six mats would be about €108 gross if justified separately.
Section 7.1.7(c) covers wire used to secure the replacement insulation. Two units benchmark at €26 gross.

Section 7.1.7(g) covers separate necessary repair hours, and the combined 13.75 technician hours broadly fit the reported day and a half. The seven-hour benchmark is €642 gross if this block is distinct repair labour rather than duplicate labour or cleaning.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows only the first travel charge for this contractor's invoice for the same repair. The conditional one-charge benchmark is €80 gross.
Section 7.1.8(b) excludes the contractor's protective equipment, and no separately attributable repair consumables are identified in the kit. The conditional estimate is €20 gross.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.7(a) cover necessary disposal of removed pipe and insulation. The closely comparable flat-rate benchmark is €60 gross.

Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.8(a) exclude general cleaning and improvement, and the combined line does not establish a need to coat the tiles. If limited removal of leak residue is separable and covered, Case 18 supports a threshold below €60; €45 gross is the estimate.
